newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt wants more talks on German petrol tax hike.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt wants more talks on German petrol tax hike.

text.p: Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday that more talks were needed in Germany's centre-right coalition government before a decision could be taken to increase petrol taxes.

"This is a subject we must discuss," Rexrodt said. He was speaking after coalition sources said a petrol tax hike was being considered to plug a gap in revenues next year resulting from the failure of parts of the 1997 tax bill.

Opposition Social Democrats (SPD), brandishing a majority in the Bundesrat upper house of parliament capable of blocking government tax measures, shot down parts of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's tax bill on Monday.

The stalemate means the wealth tax, ruled unconstitutional by a court, will be abolished from the start 1997, and rises in child benefits will go ahead automatically. Waigel says the changes would not threaten Germany's eligibility for European monetary union.
A multi-billion mark shortfall in revenues next year would only partly be made up by a rise in petrol taxes of over 10 pfennigs per litre, which the SPD said would cost motorists seven billion marks.

Rexrodt, a member of junior government partners the FDP, said there had been no result at a meeting of coalition leaders hosted earlier on Wednesday by Chancellor Helmut Kohl. He declined to give any details.
